ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The vertical axis in the attached figure is labeled p(v), and the horizontal axis is labeled v. The probability density curve starts from the origin at v=0, rises linearly with v, reaches the highest point at v=4, and has a vertical cutoff line at v=4 returning to the horizontal axis, so the pdf is a right triangle defined on 0≤v≤4. Reasoning: Let the peak height at v=4 be h. Because the total area of the probability density function must be 1, the triangle area is (1/2)·4·h=1, so h=1/2. This line passes through (0,0) and (4,1/2), and the slope is (1/2)/4=1/8, therefore p(v)=v/8, 0≤v≤4. The mean square value is E[v^2]=∫_0^4 v^2 p(v)dv=∫_0^4 v^2·(v/8)dv=(1/8)∫_0^4 v^3 dv=(1/8)·(4^4/4)=8.
